title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Effective Gravity Drainage
description: Gravity drainage relies on precise pipe slope to transport both liquids and solids efficiently. A common standard guideline for residential branch drains is a quarter-inch drop per foot of pipe run. If the pitch is too flat, wastewater flows too slowly, allowing heavy solids to settle and cause blockages. Conversely, if the pitch is excessively steep, liquids can drain away rapidly while leaving solid waste behind in the pipe. Regular inspection of pipe hangers and supports ensures lines do not sag or form low spots over time, maintaining self-cleansing velocity throughout the system.

Conversely, if the pitch is excessively steep, liquids can drain away rapidly while leaving solid waste behind in the pipe. Regular inspection of pipe hangers and supports ensures lines do not sag or form low spots over time, maintaining self-cleansing velocity throughout the system.
